quote: Was entspricht dem Hoppeschen Satz: dass in einem Tetrae- der dessen Seitenflächen gleichen Inhalt haben diese Seitenflächen nothwendig congruent sind, vergl. Hoppe Archiv Theil 12, 1893-94 im 4 oder mehr dimensionalen Raume.
english: What corresponds in 4- or more-dimensional space to Hoppe's theorem that in a tetrahedron whose faces have equal area these faces are necessarily congruent (cf. Hoppe, Archiv, Part 12, 1893-94)?
topic: Notes on deriving a theorem from the theorem on perspective triangles without continuity axioms, an analogue of Hoppe's theorem on tetrahedra with equal-area faces in four or more dimensions, and a conjecture on irreducibility of integral polynomials modulo prime powers.

triage.modern_statement: Hoppe's result, now usually called Bang's theorem on equifacial (isosceles) tetrahedra, says that if the four faces of a tetrahedron in R^3 all have the same area, then the faces are congruent. Hilbert asked what the analogue is for d-simplices with d >= 4. The direct version asks: if all d+1 facets of a d-simplex have the same (d-1)-volume, must the facets be congruent? A more general version asks: if all r-faces of a d-simplex have equal r-volume, what follows about the simplex (congruent faces, regularity)?
triage.answered_by: The direct analogue is false for d >= 4. M. Hajja and F. Saidi (Journal for Geometry and Graphics, vol. 8, Heldermann Verlag) give an explicit 4-simplex whose five tetrahedral facets have equal volumes but are not congruent. P. McMullen, 'Simplices with Equiareal Faces' (Discrete & Computational Geometry 24 (2000) 397–412), studied the general question of when equal r-volumes of r-faces force a d-simplex to be regular, and found the case r = d-2 the most fruitful. Related work continued, e.g. 'Simplices and Spectra of Graphs' (DCG 43, 2010) and the arXiv work on equifacetal simplices (math/0408132, math/0411093). None of these sources is shown to respond to Hilbert's note itself.

evidence.claim: Hajja–Saidi re-prove Bang's theorem (equal face areas imply congruent faces in a tetrahedron), then turn to higher dimensions and show there is a four-dimensional simplex whose five tetrahedral faces have equal volumes but are not congruent.

McMullen (DCG 24, 2000): for d >= 3 the facets of a d-simplex can have equal (d-1)-volume without the simplex being regular. The paper studies how far equal r-volumes of r-faces imply regularity and finds the case r = d-2 most fruitful.

Follow-up work (DCG 2010) shows that the (n-2)-volumes of codimension-2 faces of an n-simplex are algebraically independent functions of the edge lengths. It also gives families of simplices of dimension 4 or more in which the set of these (n-2)-volumes does not determine the simplex.
Survey-style arXiv work: in dimension 3, an equiareal tetrahedron has congruent faces, but in dimension d >= 4 'the situation becomes yet more complicated'.
Equifacetal simplices (all facets congruent) in higher dimensions are a studied topic, including their combinatorial types and constructions in even dimensions.

triage.why: Hilbert's question asks for the higher-dimensional form of the equal-area-implies-congruent theorem for tetrahedra. The literature I found shows the naive analogue fails from dimension 4 on, with an explicit counterexample from Hajja–Saidi. McMullen (2000) identified the right replacement: conditions on the volumes of (d-2)-faces. So the core question has an answer, and it is negative. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 published problems, and I found no source that links it to his diary. The year of the Hajja–Saidi paper is not confirmed here; the URL only shows volume 8. Later papers (2004–2010) show the topic was still being studied then, but I could not tell whether it is an active research area now.
